raw_response:
I’m 60 this year, and I’ve farmed this land a long time. I only finished middle school, so I do listen to what the township technician says, but in the end I still judge by what I saw in my own fields. Last year the wheat-maize land still gave steady grain, and cotton on part of the land helped spread the risk. That’s why I won’t change too much this year. I have 10.9 mu total, and with some people working off-farm, I can’t make the management too complicated. I’ll keep about 7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 3.9 mu in cotton. For wheat, since it is already standing at the start of the season, my main job is water and topdressing at the right time, not letting it go yellow at jointing. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is tight, so I’ll harvest wheat and seed maize right away, mostly with simple field preparation or direct seeding if I can get the machine. Cotton takes more watching for insects, but cash comes back better if the year is decent, so I’ll keep some area in it. I won’t push inputs too hard because fertilizer, water, and labor all cost money, but I also won’t cut too much because if yield falls, that hurts more.
